evidence.summary: 将DSH接入飞书/Lark，支持聊天派任务、会话与工作区切换、执行结果和人机审批卡片。
limitations: 功能摘要根据作者固定版本材料归纳，不是逐字引文或独立效果验证。

evidence.summary: 核查 README.md、package.json、src/authorization.ts、src/bridge.ts、src/clicks.ts、src/config.ts、src/credentials.ts、src/epoch.ts、src/files.ts、src/index.ts、src/liveness.ts、src/outbound-file.ts、src/permission.ts、src/provision.ts、src/runtime.ts、src/session.ts、src/workspace.ts；[Q02](#research-q02)至[Q04](#research-q04)沿SDK消息→插件授权→scope会话→Host执行/原生approval→卡片/文件回飞书核查，Host与SDK依赖分别保留。

findings.text: dsh-lark-channel是原生DSH渠道插件，同时有独立部署CLI。它把外部飞书/Lark消息变成可驱动本机Agent的入口，返回执行过程、最终答案和需人参与的卡片，支持切工作区/模型、接续会话及文件交付。适用者是已有可信DSH机器、需要离开终端继续监督任务的操作者；合格结果是原机器实际任务正确完成、审批对应真实调用、交付送到正确会话，而非机器人在线或有进度卡。
[Q02](#research-q02)至[Q04](#research-q04)沿SDK消息→插件授权→scope会话→Host执行/原生approval→卡片/文件回飞书核查，Host与SDK依赖分别保留。

核README/package、index/runtime、authorization/config、bridge入站/原生审批/决定/文件/卸载关键链、session acquire/恢复、epoch/workspace、outbound canonical/read、files下载限额、credentials、provision服务与liveness；未全审SDK、全部CLI/模型/交互卡片/原生Host。
dsh-lark-channel0.0.7原生渠道包与bin CLI，Node条件已声明；SDK为外部依赖，latest发布/租户服务本次未实时验证。

#### 启动与依赖

| 依赖或条件 | 是否必需 | 用途 | 缺失或不满足时 |
|---|---|---|---|
| DSH机器/Agent/原生工具与模型 | 必需 | 真正执行任务 | 渠道不替代沙箱/业务验收 |
| Node^22.19或>=24、飞书SDK/租户应用 | 必需 | 消息长连接 | 外部服务/权限未验，非扫码保证可用 |
| sender/group/approvers及目录收窄 | 本文试用必需 | 明确谁可驱动/批准/触及文件 | 默认群可整房授权，roots空不限制 |
| settings/credentials服务 | 持久/秘密按部署需 | state、epoch与secret引用 | 缺失可内存/secret回settings |
| 文件/视觉模型 | 文件/图像可选 | 入站落盘、出站buffer/像素推理 | 建议起步关闭，收发各有不同边界 |
| launchd/systemd | 常驻可选 | 关闭终端后运行 | 无supervisor退前台，停止需管服务 |

#### 成本

| 阶段 | 现金与资源成本 | 人工与时间投入 | 已知条件与未知项 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 首次 | 模型/机器/平台配额金额未知 | 应用/权限/成员/目录和服务配置 | 无公网回调不等无外部依赖 |
| 持续 | token/文件磁盘/buffer/消息资源未知 | 原机结果复核、卡片与升级 | 无端到端净节时实测 |
| 失败恢复 | SDK重连/重发资源未知 | 审批/Host/送达、epoch与坏历史核对 | 不明效果不盲重试 |
| 退出升级 | 凭据/设置/会话保留资源未知 | 停服务、撤应用/成员、按归属清留存 | remove不自动删secret/已发文件 |
从独立应用、非敏感目录和指定sender/group/approvers/roots的私聊只读任务开始，先关文件和图像。卡片逐项对原机调用，文件与群扩展分别核；身份或效果不明就停服务撤应用权限，回终端确认。见[Q05](#research-q05)。

#### 效果

| 效果项 | 当前证据支持 | 尚不能确定 |
|---|---|---|
| 远程参与 | 真Agent/原生卡片桥接 | 同任务质量和总人审 |
| 决定绑定 | 原chat/operator/open单次结算 | 平台延迟/重绘与Host真实时序 |
| 文件交付 | canonical和群批准固定buffer | SDK送达去重/并发文件竞态 |
| 恢复 | quota退避与epoch/会话状态 | 真实断网/坏历史无损恢复 |
消息先授权、scope状态/generation、卡片发送竞态单次结算、固定buffer群批和quota重连可借鉴；SDK/Host与成员权限是实际依赖，不能把本地receipt当跨系统业务exactly-once。
[Q01](#research-q01)、[Q03](#research-q03)、[Q04](#research-q04)支持把真实任务和原生人机决定带到聊天，并用原chat/操作者绑定、一次结算和群发送固定buffer收窄状态错配。相对只转答案有交接增量，未独立证明远程任务净收益。
[Q02](#research-q02)、[Q04](#research-q04)、[Q05](#research-q05)表明默认授权单位可为整间群，session分流不等文件租户隔离；文件默认收发、大小事后判定、secret可降级settings，且批准/Host执行/平台送达不是同一成功。部署须明确成员、目录、凭据和未决效果。
[Q06](#research-q06)提出未验证的跨Host/IM分阶段任务回执，关联批准、原生效果与送达，故障对照误判/重复外发和人审成本；SDK事实不足就保持未知，无收益则停，不计已有贡献。

technical.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01)成熟IM/SDK/DSH基线是常规渠道适配，novelty25%；[Q03](#research-q03)、[Q04](#research-q04)原生批准/卡片竞态及先buffer后群批改变正确性交接，mechanism50%；可条件迁移到其他IM审批与文件交付transfer50%，未跨渠道验证；会话/批准集中在聊天减少回终端且保留原生边界，simplification50%，成员/SDK/服务配置负担阻止更高，Q06未来回执不计。

business.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01)、[Q03](#research-q03)改变离开终端时人机审批/任务交接，workflow50%；文件和结果送IM主要是已有产物渠道便利delivery25%，不把进度卡当业务成果；[Q05](#research-q05)已有DSH机器操作者可从手机/IM监督而不远程桌面，条件性reach50%，租户/机器仍需配置非更高；未识别资源供给/收费/风险承担结构改变economics0。

recommendation.reason: 已有可信DSH机器的单用户可用独立飞书应用和非敏感workspace，指定成员与审批人后试只读远程任务。相比仅转发答案的bot，渠道能接原生会话和批准卡片，让人离开终端继续参与决定，但净节时未独立验证。出现非预期成员能驱动、批准无法对应原调用或重启后上下文不明时，用户应停服务并撤应用权限，回终端核任务，暂不重试文件或shell副作用。

scenario.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01)README7-18/68-84结合离终端→原生提问/批准→交付说明具体重复交接，超过15档仅用途推断，对已有远程监督者值得受限配置；尚无长期真实需求/原办法不足直接验收，不到30档。

advantage.rationale: [Q03](#research-q03)bridge1865-1939和[Q04](#research-q04)2076-2114支持原生批准/固定buffer交接较答案转发多实质机制，超过6档入口；SDK送达、群授权和真实任务收益未知，不到19档结果改善。

evidence.rationale: [Q02](#research-q02)至[Q05](#research-q05)覆盖消息鉴权/会话、原生approval回原promise、文件流与凭据/服务/恢复关键链，超过6档片段支持限定路径；未执行真实租户/Host，SDK内层未审，不能19档。

cost.rationale: [Q05](#research-q05)credentials122-172、provision293-316/376-384明确配置/秘密与常驻责任，非敏感受限路径可停服务撤应用回终端，超过5档退路重要不清；仍有群授权、人审/文件/升级/恢复开销且金额未知，不足15档轻负担。

publication.summaries.text: 将DSH接入飞书/Lark，支持聊天派任务、会话与工作区切换、执行结果和人机审批卡片。

items.事件监听: 飞书消息/卡片到Agent，原生approval到聊天

核心贡献 [Q01](#research-q01)、[Q03](#research-q03)、[Q04](#research-q04)支持把真实任务和原生人机决定带到聊天，并用原chat/操作者绑定、一次结算和群发送固定buffer收窄状态错配。相对只转答案有交接增量，未独立证明远程任务净收益。 ## 关键质疑 [Q02](#research-q02)、[Q04](#research-q04)、[Q05](#research-q05)表明默认授权单位可为整间群，session分流不等文件租户隔离；文件默认收发、大小事后判定、secret可降级settings，且批准/Host执行/平台送达不是同一成功。部署须明确成员、目录、凭据和未决效果。 ## 研究问题与完整回答 **插件研究总目标**：判断飞书远程渠道的身份、原生审批与文件/恢复交付边界，以及可控试用条件。 ### Q01 · 飞书渠道为谁多完成什么，相对远程聊天增量是什么？ **研究主题**：场景与需求、贡献与相对优势 #### 完整回答 dsh-lark-channel是原生DSH渠道插件，同时有独立部署CLI。它把外部飞书/Lark消息变成可驱动本机Agent的入口，返回执行过程、最终答案和需人参与的卡片，支持切工作区/模型、接续会话及文件交付。适用者是已有可信DSH机器、需要离开终端继续监督任务的操作者；合格结果是原机器实际任务正确完成、审批对应真实调用、交付送到正确会话，而非机器人在线或有进度卡。 相对只把最终答案转发到IM的bot，它接入Host已有工具/命令和审批，不要求人回终端；相对远程桌面/SSH，操作词汇和人机交接更贴聊天，却依赖飞书应用权限、成员边界与外部消息平台。Agent推理、沙箱与工具是上游DSH能力，群内多bot与轮次上限不是新多Agent算法，也不证明任务协作质量。 源码入口实际导出runtime.apply，runtime创建SDK渠道并安装bridge；资料说明用长连接、无需公网回调，但SDK服务可用与租户配置不是源码就能保证。个人所有工作都在桌面的人未必需要第二条外部入口，不能因为远程方便就忽略文件/正文经过聊天平台和可能云模型的代价。无独立真实任务/人审时间对照。 #### 证据与依据 **依据 1 · 作者声明**：[README.md:7-18](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-lark/blob/632807d9abafbb866a5e208a0298eff21c7856d1/README.md#L7-L18) 作者远程任务/卡片与CLI定位。

      "path": "README.md",
      "content": "# dsh-lark · DeepSeek Harness 飞书 / Lark 插件\n\n[![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-lark-channel)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-lark-channel) [![CI](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-lark/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-lark/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-BSD--3--Clause-blue)](LICENSE)\n\n简体中文 | [English](README.en.md)\n\n**把你正在使用的 DeepSeek Harness（DSH）接进飞书。**\n\n直接在聊天里给 Agent 派任务、看执行过程、切换工作区和模型。遇到提问、计划确认或工具审批，也不用回到终端，直接在飞书里处理。需要时，还能把多个 Agent 放进同一个群里协作。\n\n## 快速开始\n\n```sh\nnpm i -g dsh-lark-channel\ndsh-lark-channel start\n```\n\n终端会显示二维码。用飞书扫码完成应用创建，然后私聊机器人，或在群里 @ 它即可开始。\n\n启动命令会在首次安装依赖前写好 profile 的 pnpm 构建策略：未经批准的依赖构建脚本一律警告并跳过，而不是让安装失败；`protobufjs` 那个只打印提示的 postinstall 还会被按名字记为跳过。因此不需要手工执行 `pnpm approve-builds`。\n\n不想装到全局也可以直接跑，只是之后每条命令都要带 `npx`：\n\n```sh\nnpx dsh-lark-channel@latest start\n```\n\n如果还没有安装 DeepSeek Harness，先运行：\n\n```sh\nnpm i -g @deepseek-ai/dsh\n```\n\n无需公网服务器，也无需配置回调地址。\n\n## 为什么值得装\n\n- **不用守着终端**：从飞书发起任务，随时查看进度和结果。\n- **不只是聊天机器人**：可以切换真实工作区和模型，执行 Harness 已有的命令与工具。\n- **关键决定仍由你控制**：模型提问、计划审阅和工具审批都会回到当前聊天，按钮或文字都能作答。\n- **上下文不会混在一起**：不同聊天、话题和工作区可以保留各自的会话。\n- **Agent 之间也能协作**：一条命令添加更多机器人，让它们在群聊中通过 @ 交接回合，并用轮数上限防止无限对话。\n\n## 可以这样开始\n\n先看看当前状态和可用工作区：\n\n```text\n/status\n/ws\n/cd my-project\n/model\n```\n\n然后直接派一个任务：\n\n```text\n检查这个项目为什么构建失败。先给我计划，需要操作时让我确认。\n```\n\nAgent 的执行过程会显示在飞书中；需要你参与时，会发送提问、计划或审批卡片。渠道自带文案会按每位读者的飞书语言显示中文或英文。\n\n## 主要能力\n\n| 能力 | 使用体验 |\n|---|---|\n| 持久会话 | 重启后可以恢复；后续消息继续当前上下文，`/new` 可以原地重开一个 |\n| 接续已有会话 | `/sessions` 列出这个工作区里可以接续的会话——自己的历史，以及网页端/命令行开的——点一行就切过去；`/cd`、`/new` 会回到自动派生的会话 |\n| 多工作区 | `/ws` 查看、`/cd` 切换；回到原工作区时继续之前的任务 |\n| 模型切换 | `/model` 打开模型选择卡片；切换后保留当前会话，也可随时恢复默认模型 |\n| 原生执行过程 | 在飞书中查看推理、工具调用和结果，最终答案单独发送 |\n| 人机协作卡片 | 单选、多选或文字回答问题；批准计划或提出修改意见；允许或拒绝工具调用 |\n| 权限预设 | `/permission` 打开预设卡片，写明每个预设能碰到什么、会不会弹审批；放开沙箱需要审批人权限，切回更安全的预设不需要 |\n| 实时状态 | `/status` 展示工作区、模型、session 和当前权限预设；可用时还显示上下文占用与累计 token，并支持刷新 |\n| 会话隔离 | 可按聊天、话题或群成员划分独立 Agent 会话 |\n| 多 Agent 协作 | 多个机器人拥有独立设置、凭据和 session，可以在同一个群里对话与交接任务 |\n| 斜杠命令 | 宿主自带的命令（`/plan`、`/compact` 等）直接进入 DSH 命令运行时 |\n| 文件收发 | 人发文件进聊天，agent 在工作区里读；agent 的产物发回聊天，群聊里先弹审批卡 |\n\n## 常用命令\n\n| 命令 | 用途 |\n|---|---|\n| `/status` | 查看并刷新工作区、模型和 session；可用时包含上下文与 token 状态 |\n| `/ws` | 查看可用工作区 |\n| `/cd <名称或路径>` | 切换工作区 |\n| `/get <路径>` | 把工作区里的文件发到聊天 |\n| `/model` | 打开模型选择卡片 |\n| `/model use <provider/model>` | 直接切换模型 |\n| `/model reset` | 恢复默认模型 |\n| `/permission` | 打开权限预设卡片 |\n| `/permission <预设名>` | 直接切换权限预设 |\n| `/new` | 原地开一个新会话，清空上下文，工作区和模型保持不变 |\n| `/sessions` | 列出可接续的会话，点一行切过去 |\n| `/sessions <关键词>` | 按标题或 id 过滤列表 |\n| `/stop` | 停止当前任务 |\n| `/help` | 查看全部命令（含宿主提供的） |\n\n## 日常运行\n\nmacOS 和采用 systemd 的 Linux 会使用用户级后台服务，关闭终端后仍可运行：\n\n```sh\ndsh-lark-channel status\ndsh-lark-channel logs -f\ndsh-lark-channel restart\ndsh-lark-channel stop\n```\n\n用 `npx` 启动的话，这些命令同样要带 `npx dsh-lark-channel@latest` 前缀——工具会按你实际的启动方式打印提示，读到什么就能直接粘贴。\n\n升级：\n\n```sh\ndsh-lark-channel upgrade\n```\n\n它会装上最新的 CLI 并在新版本上重启机器人。用 npx 的话不需要这一步，`npx dsh-lark-channel@latest start` 本来就是最新。有新版本时，`start` 和 `status` 会顺带提醒你一行。\n\n连接异常时，插件会在限额和退避控制下自动重建 WebSocket，避免进程仍在但机器人已经静默离线。\n\n### 添加更多 Agent\n\n给第二个飞书应用添加一套独立的 Agent：\n\n```sh\ndsh-lark-channel add reviewer\n```\n\n命令会写入新实例、重启服务并显示二维码。扫码后，这个机器人拥有自己的设置、App Secret 和 session，不会与第一个机器人共享上下文。\n\n把两个机器人加入同一个群后，它们可以通过 @ 把回合交给对方。例如，让一个 Agent 完成修改后 @ 另一个 Agent 复核，后者也可以 @ 回去要求调整。默认最多连续进行 6 个机器人轮次；任何人发言都会恢复额度。需要移除时：\n\n```sh\ndsh-lark-channel remove reviewer\n```\n\n移除会保留该实例的凭据和设置，之后用同一个名字重新添加即可恢复。\n\n如果希望飞书和 `dsh web` 共用同一个 profile：\n\n```sh\ndsh plugin --profile web add dsh-lark-channel@latest\ndsh web\n```\n\n<details>\n<summary>权限与高级选项</summary>\n\n- 飞书应用的可用范围决定谁能找到机器人；`senderAllowlist`、`groupAllowlist` 和 `approvers` 可以进一步收窄权限。\n- `workspaceRoots` 可以限制聊天中允许切换到的目录。\n- `sessionScope` 支持 `chat`、`chat-thread` 和 `chat-sender` 三种会话粒度。\n- `instance` 用于命名额外的机器人实例；第一个机器人保持未命名，以兼容已有设置和会话。\n- `botPeers` 可以限制允许对话的机器人，`botHops` 控制连续机器人轮次，默认是 6。\n- 会改变状态的卡片绑定原聊天，转发到其他聊天后不能操作原会话。\n- 部署提供 credentials 服务时，扫码得到的 App Secret 会存入其中；旧版本写在 settings 中的 secret 会在下次启动时自动迁移。\n- 图片附件默认关闭；只有确认当前模型支持视觉时，才应开启 `attachImages`。\n- `receiveFiles` 默认开：入站文件落在当前会话工作区的 `.dsh-lark/inbox/<时间戳>-<消息哈希>/` 下，只增不删，清理是你的决定；首次落地时会提醒把 `.dsh-lark/` 加进 `.gitignore`，但不会替你去改这个文件。\n- `sendFiles` 默认开：私聊直接发，群聊每次弹审批卡片，卡片上是文件在工作区内的位置、工作区名和大小（不是宿主的绝对路径——群里每个人都会看到它）；**没有关闭群聊审批的开关**，因为那会是提示注入外泄链的官方后门。\n- 出站文件的路径一律只说\"工作区内的相对位置\"，宿主绝对前缀不会出现在任何一句给人或给模型看的话里——包括读取失败时文件系统自己那句报错（`/get` 的回复和 `send_file` 给模型的报错都在内）。失败分支恰恰是提示注入能主动触发的那条。\n- 一个群同时最多挂 3 个待审文件：群聊发送会在问群之前就把整个文件读进内存，好让群里批的和最终发出去的是同一份，所以待审数量必须有上限。第 4 次会被直接拒绝并告诉模型等前面几个先有结果。这个数字不可配置，调大等于同时买回内存风险和审批疲劳。\n- 审批结束卡会记录决定人：回调未带姓名时，渠道会尽力从当前聊天成员名单解析；没有成员查询权限、查询失败或成员已不在群内时仍安全显示 open_id，绝不会影响审批或文件发送。\n- 单文件上限默认 20 MiB，收发分别由 `maxReceiveFileBytes` /       "content": "/**\n * Who may drive this channel's agents and answer their approval questions.\n *\n * The platform owns the outer boundary. An app's visibility scope decides who\n * in the tenant can reach the bot at all — for direct messages that IS the\n * authorization decision, made in the developer console — and a group is a room\n * someone deliberately put the bot in. This plugin therefore narrows rather\n * than gates: every list here is empty by default and only restricts when a\n * deployment fills it in.\n * @module dsh-lark-channel/authorization\n */\n\nimport type { ResolvedConfig } from './config.ts'\n\n/** The narrowing rules one running channel applies. */\nexport interface Authorization {\n  /** Senders allowed to send direct messages; empty allows everyone the platform admits. */\n  readonly directSenders: ReadonlySet<string>\n  /** Group chat ids the channel serves; empty serves any group the bot is in. */\n  readonly groups: ReadonlySet<string>\n  /** Open ids that may answer approvals; empty lets anyone who may drive the chat answer. */\n  readonly approvers: ReadonlySet<string>\n  /** Bot open ids answered; empty narrows nothing, as every list here does. */\n  readonly botPeers: ReadonlySet<string>\n  /** Consecutive bot-sourced turns one conversation may run. */\n  readonly botHops: number\n}\n\n/**\n * Resolve the narrowing rules from configuration.\n * @param config - resolved plugin configuration.\n * @returns the channel's authorization rules.\n */\nexport function resolveAuthorization(config: ResolvedConfig): Authorization {\n  return {\n    directSenders: new Set(config.senderAllowlist),\n    groups: new Set(config.groupAllowlist),\n    approvers: new Set(config.approvers),\n    botPeers: new Set(config.botPeers),\n    botHops: config.botHops,\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * State the channel's reach once, for the operator, at startup — who it will\n * serve is a fact worth seeing next to the fact that it runs a shell.\n * @param authorization - the channel's authorization rules.\n * @returns one console line describing that reach.\n */\nexport function describeAuthorization(authorization: Authorization): string {\n  const direct = authorization.directSenders.size === 0\n    ? 'direct messages: anyone the app is visible to (narrow with senderAllowlist)'\n    : `direct messages: ${[...authorization.directSenders].join(', ')}`\n  const groups = authorization.groups.size === 0\n    ? 'groups: any group the bot is added to, when @-mentioned'\n    : `groups: ${[...authorization.groups].join(', ')}`\n  const approvers = authorization.approvers.size === 0\n    ? 'approvals: anyone who may drive that chat'\n    : `approvals: ${[...authorization.approvers].join(', ')}`\n  const bots = authorization.botPeers.size === 0\n    ? `bots: any bot in a chat it serves, up to ${authorization.botHops} consecutive turns (narrow with botPeers)`\n    : `bots: ${[...authorization.botPeers].join(', ')}, up to ${authorization.botHops} consecutive turns`\n  return `lark-channel: ${direct}; ${groups}; ${approvers}; ${bots}`\n}\n\n/** One inbound message's authorization subject. */\nexport interface MessageSubject {\n  readonly senderId: string\n  readonly chatId: string\n  readonly chatType: string\n}\n\n/**\n * Whether one inbound message may drive this channel.\n * @param authorization - the channel's authorization rules.\n * @param subject - the message's sender, chat, and chat kind.\n * @returns the refusal reason for the operator log, or undefined when allowed.\n */\nexport function refuseMessage(\n  authorization: Authorization,\n  subject: MessageSubject,\n): string | undefined {\n  if (subject.chatType === 'p2p') {\n    if (authorization.directSenders.size === 0) return undefined\n    return authorization.directSenders.has(subject.senderId)\n      ? undefined\n      : `sender ${subject.senderId} is not in senderAllowlist`\n  }\n  // Group members are not gated individually: someone chose to put the bot in\n  // this room, and `requireMention` already decides what counts as addressing it.\n  if (authorization.groups.size > 0 && !authorization.groups.has(subject.chatId)) {\n    return `group ${subject.chatId} is not in groupAllowlist`\n  }\n  return undefined\n}\n\n/**\n * Whether one card click may settle an approval. With no configured approvers,\n * whoever may drive that chat may also answer it — in a group that is the room.\n * Narrow it with `approvers` when an escalation should need a named human.\n * @param authorization - the channel's authorization rules.\n * @param click - the clicking operator, and the chat the click came from.\n * @param pending - the chat the approval card was published to, and its kind.\n * @returns the refusal reason, or undefined when the click counts.\n */\nexport function refuseApprovalClick(\n  authorization: Authorization,\n  click: { readonly operatorId: string | undefined; readonly chatId: string },\n  pending: { readonly chatId: string; readonly chatType: string },\n): string | undefined {\n  // The card carries its own correlation id, so a click from elsewhere did not\n  // come from the card this question published.\n  if (click.chatId !== pending.chatId) {\n    return `click from chat ${click.chatId} does not match the card's chat ${pending.chatId}`\n  }\n  if (click.operatorId === undefined) return 'the click carries no operator id'\n  if (authorization.approvers.size > 0) {\n    return authorization.approvers.has(click.operatorId)\n      ? undefined\n      : `operator ${click.operatorId} is not in approvers`\n  }\n  return refuseMessage(authorization, {\n    senderId: click.operatorId,\n    chatId: pending.chatId,\n    chatType: pending.chatType,\n  })\n}\n"

      "path": "src/credentials.ts",
      "content": "/**\n * Where this channel's app secret lives.\n *\n * The host owns a seam for exactly this: `ctx.credentials` resolves a\n * REFERENCE — a shell-identifier name like `LARK_APP_SECRET` — through\n * whichever provider a deployment composed, reading an environment variable,\n * a dotenv file, or its own store, and reporting changes so the next\n * operation picks them up. Configuration surfaces then describe a secret\n * without ever holding one.\n *\n * This plugin used to persist the scanned secret straight into the user\n * settings document, which is the wrong home for it twice over: that document\n * is meant to be read and hand-edited, and it is the same file a deployment\n * copies around to move its preferences. The secret now goes to the\n * credentials seam and the settings keep only the reference.\n *\n * A deployment without a credentials provider keeps working exactly as it\n * did, secret and all — degrading to a worse hiding place beats refusing to\n * onboard a bot.\n * @module dsh-lark-channel/credentials\n */\n\n/** Where a resolved credential came from, as the provider reports it. */\nexport interface ResolvedCredential {\n  readonly value: string\n  /** `env`, `file`, or a dotenv path — an operator's answer to \"which one is live?\". */\n  readonly source?: string\n}\n\n/** The `credentials` seam, narrowed to what this plugin does with it. */\nexport interface HostCredentials {\n  /**\n   * Read one reference's current value.\n   * @param ref - the reference name.\n   * @returns the value and its source, or undefined when nothing is stored.\n   */\n  resolve(ref: string): Promise<ResolvedCredential | undefined>\n  /**\n   * Store one reference's value.\n   * @param ref - the reference name.\n   * @param value - the secret; providers reject an empty one.\n   */\n  set(ref: string, value: string): Promise<void>\n}\n\n/**\n * The reference this channel stores its app secret under.\n *\n * Deliberately the same name as the environment variable the provisioning CLI\n * writes: a deployment that exports `LARK_APP_SECRET` is already configured,\n * because the local provider resolves an inherited environment variable before\n * anything it stores itself.\n */\nexport const APP_SECRET_REF = 'LARK_APP_SECRET'\n\n/** A reference must be a shell identifier; the seam brands them that way. */\nconst REF_PATTERN = /^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$/\n\n/**\n * Whether a configured reference is one the seam will accept.\n * @param ref - the candidate reference.\n * @returns whether it is a shell identifier.\n */\nexport function isCredentialRef(ref: string): boolean {\n  return REF_PATTERN.test(ref)\n}\n\n/**\n * Resolve the app secret for one configuration.\n *\n * A secret written into the entry config wins: a deployment that injected it\n * (from its own environment, its own vault) has said where the value comes\n * from, and reaching past that to a stored reference would silently serve a\n * different bot than the composition asked for.\n * @param credentials - the seam, when a provider is composed.\n * @param config - the app id, the inline secret, and the reference.\n * @param report - operator console line for a reference that cannot resolve.\n * @returns the secret, or undefined when neither source has one.\n */\nexport async function resolveAppSecret(\n  credentials: HostCredentials | undefined,\n  config: { readonly appSecret?: string | undefined; readonly appSecretRef?: string | undefined },\n  report: (line: string) => void,\n): Promise<string | undefined> {\n  if (config.appSecret !== undefined && config.appSecret !== '') return config.appSecret\n  const ref = config.appSecretRef\n  if (ref === undefined || ref === '') return undefined\n  if (!isCredentialRef(ref)) {\n    report(`lark-channel: appSecretRef \"${ref}\" is not a valid credential reference; ignoring it`)\n    return undefined\n  }\n  if (credentials === undefined) {\n    report(`lark-channel: no credentials provider is composed, so appSecretRef \"${ref}\" cannot be resolved`)\n    return undefined\n  }\n  const resolved = await credentials.resolve(ref).catch((error: unknown) => {\n    report(`lark-channel: resolving credential \"${ref}\" failed: ${String(error)}`)\n    return undefined\n  })\n  if (resolved === undefined || resolved.value === '') {\n    report(`lark-channel: credential \"${ref}\" is not configured`)\n    return undefined\n  }\n  return resolved.value\n}\n\n/** What became of an attempt to put a secret behind a reference. */\nexport interface SecretStored {\n  /** The reference to record in settings, when the secret was stored behind one. */\n  readonly ref?: string\n  /** Whether the secret itself still has to be written to settings. */\n  readonly inSettings: boolean\n}\n\n/**\n * Store one app secret in the best home this deployment offers.\n * @param credentials - the seam, when a provider is composed.\n * @param secret - the secret to store.\n * @param report - operator console line.\n * @returns the reference to record, or the instruction to keep the secret in settings.\n */\nexport async function storeAppSecret(\n  credentials: HostCredentials | undefined,\n  secret: string,\n  report: (line: string) => void,\n  ref: string = APP_SECRET_REF,\n): Promise<SecretStored> {\n  if (credentials === undefined) return { inSettings: true }\n  try {\n    await credentials.set(ref, secret)\n    return { ref, inSettings: false }\n  } catch (error) {\n    // Worth a line rather than a throw: a bot that onboarded is more use than\n    // one that refused to, and the operator can move the secret later.\n    report(`lark-channel: storing the app secret as \"${ref}\" failed (${String(error)}); keeping it in settings`)\n    return { inSettings: true }\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Move a secret already sitting in the settings document behind a reference.\n *\n * Runs on every boot that finds one there, so a deployment onboarded before\n * this existed is repaired by restarting rather than by re-scanning. The\n * settings value is blanked rather than deleted, because a deep-merge patch\n * cannot remove a key — and an empty secret is an absent one everywhere here.\n * @param credentials - the seam, when a provider is composed.\n * @param config - the configuration as the settings document resolved it.\n * @param persist - the settings patch writer.\n * @param report - operator console line.\n * @returns the reference the secret now lives behind, when it moved.\n */\nexport async function migrateAppSecret(\n  credentials: HostCredentials | undefined,\n  config: { readonly appSecret?: string | undefined; readonly appSecretRef?: string | undefined },\n  persist: (patch: object) => Promise<boolean>,\n  report: (line: string) => void,\n  ref: string = APP_SECRET_REF,\n): Promise<string | undefined> {\n  const secret = config.appSecret\n  if (secret === undefined || secret === '') return undefined\n  if (credentials === undefined) return undefined\n  const stored = await storeAppSecret(credentials, secret, report, ref)\n  if (stored.ref === undefined) return undefined\n  const persisted = await persist({ appSecret: '', appSecretRef: stored.ref }).catch((error: unknown) => {\n    report(`lark-channel: moving the app secret out of settings failed: ${String(error)}`)\n    return false\n  })\n  if (!persisted) return undefined\n  report(`lark-channel: moved the app secret out of user settings; it is now the credential \"${stored.ref}\"`)\n  return stored.ref\n}\n"

      "content": "/**\n * Starting over in the same place.\n *\n * A conversation's session id is derived, not allocated: the same chat (and,\n * after `/cd`, the same directory) resolves to the same id on every boot,\n * which is what lets a restarted process pick a conversation back up. That\n * leaves nothing to vary when someone wants a FRESH context without moving\n * anywhere — the reason `/new` did not exist.\n *\n * An epoch is that varying part: a small integer per (conversation ×\n * directory), stored beside the workspace and model maps and folded into the\n * id. Absent means zero, and zero derives exactly the id it always did, so no\n * stored conversation moves and nothing needs migrating.\n *\n * It is per directory rather than per conversation on purpose: `/cd` already\n * gives each directory its own thread, and resetting the thread you are in\n * should not silently discard the one you would return to.\n *\n * Nothing is deleted. A session log is written when an agent is created, so an\n * epoch nobody speaks into costs nothing at all, and the previous session\n * stays on disk where the host's own tools can still reach it — a chat command\n * should not be able to destroy a record.\n * @module dsh-lark-channel/epoch\n */\n\n/** Start a fresh session for this conversation. Channel-owned: needs no agent. */\nexport const NEW_COMMAND = 'new'\n\n/** Entry value marking \"explicitly the first epoch\": a deep-merged patch cannot delete a key. */\nconst DEFAULT_MARKER = ''\n\n/** Construction options for {@link ChatEpochs}. */\nexport interface ChatEpochsOptions {\n  /** Persisted base-session-id → epoch; {@link DEFAULT_MARKER} means the first. */\n  readonly entries?: Record<string, string> | undefined\n  /** Deep-merge one patch into the plugin's settings section; false = not composed. */\n  readonly persist?: ((patch: { chatEpochs: Record<string, string> }) => Promise<boolean>) | undefined\n  /** Operator console line. */\n  readonly report?: ((line: string) => void) | undefined\n}\n\n/** What one `/new` concluded. */\nexport interface EpochChange {\n  /** The epoch the conversation now runs on. */\n  readonly epoch: number\n  /** Whether the move survives a restart. */\n  readonly durable: boolean\n}\n\n/**\n * How many times each conversation has started over, keyed by the session id\n * it would derive at epoch zero. Pure state plus injected persistence,\n * mirroring the workspace and model stores.\n */\nexport class ChatEpochs {\n  private readonly entries: Map<string, string>\n  private readonly persist: (patch: { chatEpochs: Record<string, string> }) => Promise<boolean>\n  private readonly report: (line: string) => void\n  /** The non-durable warning is orientation; once is enough. */\n  private warnedNotDurable = false\n\n  constructor(options: ChatEpochsOptions = {}) {\n    this.entries = new Map(Object.entries(options.entries ?? {}))\n    this.persist = options.persist ??       "content": "/**\n * How bytes leave a workspace for the chat: the model's own `send_file`, the\n * human's `/get`, and the one check both go through.\n *\n * This module exists in this shape because of HOW the bytes leave. The plugin\n * hands the transport a `Buffer` rather than a local path (ADR 0004), and\n * `MediaUploader.toBuffer` returns on its first line for a buffer —\n * `Buffer.isBuffer(source)` — so the SDK's own\n * `resolve → blacklist → realpath → re-check → allowlist` guard never runs for\n * anything this plugin sends. What this\n   * names is the object the container check cleared, minus a prefix that says\n   * nothing about it.\n   */\n  readonly pathInWorkspace: string\n  /**\n   * The workspace's own name, i.e. the canonical workspace directory's basename.\n   * Enough to tell one conversation's workspace from another's without printing\n   * the operator's home directory.\n   */\n  readonly workspaceName: string\n}\n\n/** What one path turned out to be: a file cleared to leave, or a refusal. */\nexport type OutboundVerdict =\n  | { readonly ok: true; readonly file: OutboundFile }\n  | { readonly ok: false; readonly refusal: OutboundRefusal }\n\n/**\n * What one workspace directory is called.\n * @param container - the canonical workspace directory.\n * @returns its basename, or the directory itself when it has none — a workspace\n * mounted at a filesystem root, whose name would otherwise come out empty.\n */\nfunction workspaceNameOf(container: string): string {\n  const name = basename(container)\n  return name === '' ? container : name\n}\n\n/**\n * What the filesystem says about one canonical path.\n * @param path - a canonical path.\n * @returns whether it is a regular file and how big, or undefined when it cannot be examined.\n */\nfunction inspectFile(path: string): { readonly isFile: boolean; readonly bytes: number } | undefined {\n  try {\n    const stats = statSync(path)\n    return { isFile: stats.isFile(), bytes: stats.size }\n  } catch {\n    return undefined\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Whether one path may leave this workspace, and what it weighs.\n *\n * The order of the steps IS the check, and it is the order the SDK itself walks\n * for a local path — the one this plugin steps around by handing over a\n * `Buffer` (see the module note). Resolve, canonicalize, and only THEN ask\n * whether the result is inside the workspace: swap the last two and\n * `<workspace>/link → /etc/shadow` clears the container check, because the\n * question would be about the link's own path and not about the bytes it points\n * at. **Do not reorder those two.**\n *\n * The workspace is canonicalized too, or macOS — where `/tmp` is a link into\n * `/private/var` — would judge every file in it an escape.\n * @param input - the path as its caller typed it; a relative one resolves against the workspace.\n * @param workspace - the conversation's workspace, the only directory bytes may come from.\n * @param maxBytes - the single-file ceiling.\n * @returns the cleared file, or why it is refused.\n */\nexport function resolveOutboundFile(input: string, workspace: string, maxBytes: number): OutboundVerdict {\n  const requested = input.trim()\n  // Naming no file at all is not \"the workspace is not a file\" — which is what\n  // resolving an empty path against it would conclude — it is a missing path.\n  if (requested === '') return { ok: false, refusal: { code: 'not_found' } }\n  // A workspace that cannot be canonicalized still bounds the check: its\n  // resolved form is what every path under it will be compared against.\n  const container = canonicalPathOf(workspace) ?? resolve(workspace)\n  const canonical = canonicalPathOf(resolve(container, requested))\n  if (canonical === undefined) return { ok: false, refusal: { code: 'not_found' } }\n  if (!isWithinContainer(canonical, container)) return { ok: false, refusal: { code: 'outside_workspace' } }\n  const found = inspectFile(canonical)\n  if (found === undefined) return { ok: false, refusal: { code: 'not_found' } }\n  if (!found.isFile) return { ok: false, refusal: { code: 'not_a_file' } }\n  if (found.bytes > maxBytes) {\n    return { ok: false, refusal: { code: 'too_large', bytes: found.bytes, limit: maxBytes } }\n  }\n  return {\n    ok: true,\n    file: {\n      path: canonical,\n      fileName: basename(canonical),\n      bytes: found.bytes,\n      pathInWorkspace: relative(container, canonical),\n      workspaceName: workspaceNameOf(container),\n    },\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Read the cleared file's bytes for `send({ file })`.\n *\n * The bytes come from the verdict's canonical path and never from the caller's\n * own input, so a link the check already followed cannot be followed a second\n * time to somewhere else.\n *\n * The size is checked again against the verdict, because `readFile` treats the\n * size it stats as a hint and reads to EOF regardless. A file still being\n * appended to when it was cleared — an agent's own background process writing\n * on — would otherwise come back BIGGER than the ceiling that just let it\n * through, and the ceiling is the whole reason this function exists.\n *\n * That check enforces the CEILING and closes no race: a rewrite to the same\n * length passes it unnoticed, and this function re-examines neither the\n * canonical path nor what it now points at. So it is not what makes a group's\n * approval mean anything — the caller's ORDER is. `deliverFile` reads the bytes\n * before it asks the room and sends the buffer it already holds, so the file the\n * card certified is the object that leaves.\n * @param file - a file {@link resolveOutboundFile} cleared.\n * @returns its contents.\n * @throws {Error} when the file vanished after it was cleared, or is no longer the size it cleared at.\n */\nexport async function readOutboundFile(file: OutboundFile): Promise<Buffer> {\n  const bytes = await readFile(file.path)\n  if (bytes.byteLength !== file.bytes) throw new Error(`${file.fileName} changed size after it was cleared`)\n  return bytes\n}\n\n/**\n * Why a cleared file could not be read, said without spelling the host's path.\n *\n * `readFile`'s own failures quote the absolute path they were handed —\n * `ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/Users/…/project/out/a.md'` — so\n * passing one straight through undoes in the failure branch exactly what every\n * other branch here is careful about: the model gets a map of the filesystem it\n * never typed, and a chat reply hands the same map to a whole room. The failure\n * branch is if anything the likelier one to be read by a stranger, because it is\n * the branch an injected instruction can provoke on purpose.\n *\n * The workspace prefix is cut rather than the whole path, so what a reader gets\n * is the file's place inside the workspace and the reason it failed — `open\n * 'out/a.md'`, still enough to act on. Both audiences share this one sentence:\n * the technical detail is the same in either language, and a second copy of the\n * scrub is a second place to forget it.\n * @param error - the rejection from {@link readOutboundFile}.\n * @param file - the file it was reading.\n * @returns the reason, carrying no absolute path.\n */\nexport function describeReadFailure(error: unknown, file: OutboundFile): string {\n  const detail = failureDetail(error)\n  // Recovered from the two forms the verdict already holds rather than passed in\n  // again: `<container>/` is exactly what the canonical path has and the\n  // workspace-relative one does not.\n  const prefix = file.path.slice(0, file.path.length - file.pathInWorkspace.length)\n  return prefix === '' ? detail : detail.replaceAll(prefix, '')\n}\n\n/**\n * The refusal as the model reads it — English, actionable, and naming no path\n * the model did not supply itself. Use it for artifacts: reports, diffs, generated images, exported data. Short content '\n  + 'belongs in your reply instead — never send a file just to say a few sentences. One call sends one file; '\n  + 'call it again for more.'\n\n/** What the tool needs from the bridge to send one file. */\nexport interface SendFilePorts {\n  /**\n   * Deliver one cleared file to the agent's own chat, gate included.\n   * @param sessionId - the agent's session, which names the chat.\n   * @param file - the file the check cleared.\n   * @param signal - the execution's cancellation. Passed on because a gate can\n   * outlive the call that opened it: a group approval waits for a human, and\n   * without this the card left behind by a cancelled turn stays live for the\n   * whole approval timeout — someone pressing \"allow\" twenty minutes after the\n   * turn was stopped would put the file in the group anyway, which is the leak\n   * the gate exists to prevent (ADR 0002).\n   * @returns undefined on success, or the reason the send did not happen.\n   */\n  deliver(sessionId: string, file: OutboundFile, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<string | undefined>\n  /**\n   * The conversation workspace one session runs in, or undefined when it has no chat.\n   * @param sessionId - the agent's session.\n   * @returns the workspace directory, or undefined.\n   */\n  workspaceOf(sessionId: string): string | undefined\n  /** The single-file ceiling. */\n  readonly maxBytes: number\n  /**\n   * Operator console line. A path this check refuses never reaches\n   * {@link SendFilePorts.deliver}, so this is the only place an attempt to leave\n   * the workspace can be reported — and an escape attempt is an operator's\n   * event, not just the model's error.\n   */\n  readonly report: (line: string) => void\n}\n\n/**\n * Build the agent-scoped `send_file`.\n *\n * Every refusal is thrown rather than returned, as in `plan.ts`: a tool result\n * is what steers the model's next move, and \"that file is too big\" has to reach\n * it as a failure it must act on rather than a field it may ignore.\n * @param ports - how to look up the workspace and deliver the bytes.\n * @returns the definition, for `tools.register` on an agent's context.\n */\nexport function sendFileTool(ports: SendFilePorts): object {\n  return {\n    name: SEND_FILE_TOOL,\n    description: SEND_FILE_DESCRIPTION,\n    parameters: {\n      type: 'object',\n      required: ['path'],\n      properties: {\n        path: { type: 'string', description: 'Path to the file, inside the workspace.' },\n      },\n    },\n    output: {\n      schema: {\n        type: 'object',\n        additionalProperties: false,\n        required: ['sent'],\n        properties: { sent: { type: 'boolean' } },\n      },\n      render: () => [{ type: 'text', text: 'The file was sent to the chat.' }],\n    },\n    async execute(args: unknown, exec: unknown): Promise<{ sent: true }> {\n      // Total by construction: without `defineTool`'s validating wrapper this\n      // body IS the validation, and a path-shaped argument that is not a string\n      // must reach the ordinary refusal rather than throw a type error.\n      const requested = String((args as { path?: unknown } | null | undefined)?.path ?? '')\n      const context = exec as { agent?: { session?: { id?: string } }; signal?: AbortSignal }\n      const sessionId = context.agent?.session?.id\n      if (sessionId === undefined) {\n        throw new Error(`${SEND_FILE_TOOL} requires a calling agent (no chat to send a file to)`)\n      }\n      const workspace = ports.workspaceOf(sessionId)\n      if (workspace === undefined) {\n        throw new Error(`${SEND_FILE_TOOL} found no chat for this session, so there is nowhere to send a file`)\n      }\n      const verdict = resolveOutboundFile(requested, workspace, ports.maxBytes)\n      if (!verdict.ok) {\n        // The ESCAPE is reported, and only the escape. A model reaching outside\n        // its workspace is the shape an injected instruction takes, it never\n        // reaches the delivery port, so this is the only place it can leave a\n        // trace — while \"not found\", \"not a file\" and \"too large\" are the model\n        // mistyping a path or misjudging a size, and putting those on the\n        // console lets a model that keeps guessing write to it at will.\n        // Collapsed to one bounded line first, because the path is model-authored\n        // text and a console line it could break in two is one it could forge.\n        if (verdict.refusal.code === 'outside_workspace') {\n          const attempted = requested.replace(/\\s+/g, ' ').slice(0, 200)\n          ports.report(`lark-channel: ${SEND_FILE_TOOL} refused ${attempted} `\n            + `in session ${sessionId}: ${verdict.refusal.code}`)\n        }\n        throw new Error(describeRefusalForModel(verdict.refusal))\n      }\n      // Refused by its human, timed out, upload failed: one string, because to\n      // the model they are one thing — the file did not arrive, and why.       "path": "src/permission.ts",
      "content": "/**\n * The permission preset, as a thing a chat can see and change.\n *\n * The host owns both knobs — how far the sandbox lets a command reach, and\n * whether an action that needs approval gets to ask — and pairs them into\n * named presets switched by `/permission <name>`. The command already takes\n * that argument; a chat could always switch, it just had to know the name and\n * type it. So this module is not new capability, it is the same capability\n * with a surface: read the current preset, offer the others, and switch by\n * running the host's own command.\n *\n * One property of the shipped table has to reach the person pressing the\n * button. `danger-full-access` is not only \"stop confining\" — it also sets the\n * approval policy to `never`, and `never` means an action that still needs\n * approval is REFUSED rather than waved through. Someone who reads the name as\n * \"allow everything\" would be half right and half wrong, which is the worst\n * way to be wrong about a permission.\n * @module dsh-lark-channel/permission\n */\n\nimport type { HostAgent, HostCommands, HostPermissionPresets, HostSessionProjections } from './host.ts'\nimport type { ConversationSubject } from './session.ts'\n\n/**\n * The `permissions` projection the host publishes for every session: which\n * preset is in force and which ones exist.\n */\nexport interface PermissionsProjection {\n  readonly currentValue?: unknown\n  readonly options?: readonly {\n    readonly value?: unknown\n    readonly name?: unknown\n    readonly description?: unknown\n  }[]\n}\n\n/**\n * One preset a deployment offers, as the host describes it.\n *\n * The host names and explains its own presets, including ones a deployment\n * added. Keeping only the value would leave a card able to explain exactly the\n * two names this plugin happens to hardcode.\n */\nexport interface PresetOption {\n  /** The name `/permission` takes, and what a button carries. */\n  readonly value: string\n  /** What to show a reader; the value itself when the host offered no other. */\n  readonly name: string\n  /** The host's own explanation, when it published one. */\n  readonly description?: string | undefined\n  /**\n   * What the preset actually does, from the deployment's own table.\n   *\n   * Carried so that what a card SAYS and what this channel ENFORCES read the\n   * same source. A deployment defines its own table: a preset called\n   * `workspace-write` can be unconfined underneath, and a card that described\n   * it from the name would be asking someone to authorize one thing while\n   * granting another — in the one place where that is least acceptable, a\n   * consent screen. Absent when the table cannot be read.\n   */\n  readonly sandbox?: string | undefined\n  readonly approval?: string | undefined\n}\n\n/** The host command that switches presets. Channel-driven, host-owned. */\nexport const PERMISSION_COMMAND = 'permission'\n\n/** Marks this plugin's preset buttons apart from other card actions. */\nexport const PERMISSION_ACTION = 'dsh-lark-channel/permission'\n\n/** The preset this channel treats as the loud one, whatever else a deployment defines. */\nexport const UNCONFINED_PRESET = 'danger-full-access'\n\n/** What one conversation's presets look like right now. */\nexport interface PresetState {\n  /** The preset in force, when the host reported one. */\n  readonly current?: string | undefined\n  /** Every preset this deployment offers, in the host's own order. */\n  readonly available: readonly PresetOption[]\n}\n\n/**\n * Whether switching to one preset loosens what the conversation may reach.\n *\n * The one asymmetry this channel's authorization rests on: taking the sandbox\n * off is a grant, and putting it back on is not. A rule that gated both the\n * same way would stop an ordinary member from making their own conversation\n * SAFER, which is the wrong thing to make hard.\n *\n * Judged by what the preset DOES, not by what it is called.       "content": "/**\n * Durable, scope-aware conversation sessions. One conversation facet — the\n * whole chat, one topic thread, or one sender inside a chat — owns exactly one\n * agent session whose id is derived from that facet alone, so a restarted\n * process reaches the conversation's stored session instead of starting it over\n * and a topic group no longer funnels every thread into one agent.\n * @module dsh-lark-channel/session\n */\n\nimport type { NormalizedMessage } from '@larksuite/channel'\nimport { failureDetail } from './format.ts'\nimport type { HostAgentHandle } from './host.ts'\n\n/** Which conversation facet owns one agent session. */\nexport type SessionScope = 'chat' | 'chat-thread' | 'chat-sender'\n\n/**\n * Marks a session id as this channel's, in the host agent registry and in the\n * on-disk session log. Stable: changing it orphans every stored conversation.\n */\nexport const SESSION_PREFIX = 'lark-'\n\n/** Separator between a conversation key's facets; absent from Feishu open ids. */\nconst FACET_SEPARATOR = ':'\n\n/**\n * A walk finished under a generation that a release had already moved past.\n * Not a failure of the conversation — the waiter simply retries under the new\n * state — so it must be distinguishable from a real creation error, which is\n * reported to the chat.\n */\nclass SupersededError extends Error {\n  constructor(key: string) {\n    super(`lark-channel: opening for ${key} was superseded by a release`)\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Which conversation a control card governs, and where it was published.\n *\n * A card that changes a conversation's settings has to say which conversation\n * it means, because a click arrives with only a chat and an operator — not the\n * thread or the sender facet the key was derived from. The chat is carried so\n * a FORWARDED card cannot act: the same payload pressed in another room no\n * longer matches the room the card was published to.\n */\nexport interface ConversationSubject {\n  /** The conversation key, from {@link conversationKey}. */\n  readonly key: string\n  /** The chat the card was published to. */\n  readonly chatId: string\n  /** That chat's kind, so a click is authorized exactly as a message is. */\n  readonly chatType: string\n  /** The only operator the click may come from, when the scope is per-sender. */\n  readonly owner?: string | undefined\n}\n\n/**\n * Derive the stable conversation key one session owns. Pure: the same\n * conversation facet yields the same key in every process.\n * @param scope - the facet a session is bound to.\n * @param msg - normalized inbound chat message.\n * @returns the conversation key.\n * @throws {Error} when `scope` is outside {@link SessionScope}.\n */\nexport function conversationKey(scope: SessionScope, msg: NormalizedMessage): string {\n  switch (scope) {\n    case 'chat':\n      return msg.chatId\n    case 'chat-thread':\n      // Only a topic group splits into threads; an ordinary group carries none,\n      // and there the whole chat is the finest facet available.\n      return msg.threadId === undefined\n        ? msg.chatId\n        : `${msg.chatId}${FACET_SEPARATOR}${msg.threadId}`\n    case 'chat-sender':\n      return `${msg.chatId}${FACET_SEPARATOR}${msg.senderId}`\n    default: {\n      const unhandled: never = scope\n      throw new Error(`lark-channel: unknown session scope ${String(unhandled)}`)\n    }\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Brand a conversation key as the session id that owns it. Concatenation only,\n * so the mapping is injective by construction: two conversations can never\n * share one session, and one conversation resolves to the same durable session\n * on every boot.\n * @param key - a conversation key from {@link conversationKey}.\n * @returns the session id to look up, resume, or create.\n */\nexport function sessionIdFor(key: string, prefix: string = SESSION_PREFIX): string {\n  return `${prefix}${key}`\n}\n\n/** One agent this channel drives, and whether disposing it is this channel's job. */\nexport interface OpenedSession {\n  readonly handle: HostAgentHandle\n  /** False when the agent was already live under another owner. */\n  readonly owned: boolean\n}\n\n/**\n * Host operations the ladder needs, as plain functions: the host `agents`\n * registry satisfies them through the bridge, while tests substitute an\n * in-memory object and need no Cordis mount.\n */\nexport interface SessionLadder {\n  /**\n   * Return the live agent for this id, if the host already has one.\n   * @param sessionId - the branded session id.\n   * @returns the live handle, or undefined when nothing runs on that id.\n   */\n  lookup(sessionId: string): HostAgentHandle | undefined\n  /**\n   * Load a persisted session as a live agent.\n   * @param sessionId - the branded session id.\n   * @returns the resumed handle.\n   * @throws when no session is stored under the id, or its log cannot be read.\n   */\n  resume(sessionId: string): Promise<HostAgentHandle>\n  /**\n   * Create a fresh agent on this id.\n   * @param sessionId - the branded session id.\n   * @returns the created handle.\n   * @throws when the agent cannot be composed.\n   */\n  create(sessionId: string): Promise<HostAgentHandle>\n  /**\n   * Report a failure that is handled rather than propagated. The line is\n   * operator-facing and self-describing.\n   * @param line - the complete report line.\n   */\n  report(line: string): void\n}\n\n/**\n * Get, resume, or create the agent bound to one conversation key, deduplicated\n * per key so a burst of messages cannot race two sessions into existence.\n * Bindings live until {@link ConversationSessions.close}, which disposes every\n * agent this store owns.\n */\nexport class ConversationSessions {\n  /** Resolved sessions by conversation key. */\n  private readonly opened = new Map<string, OpenedSession>()\n  /** Conversation key per live session id, in binding order. */\n  private readonly keys = new Map<string, string>()\n  /** Acquisitions still walking the ladder, joined by concurrent messages. */\n  private readonly opening = new Map<string, Promise<OpenedSession>>()\n  /**\n   * Release epoch per key. A release advances it SYNCHRONOUSLY before any\n   * await, so every walk that started earlier can tell its result is stale —\n   * a waiter that merely joined a shared opening promise would otherwise be\n   * handed the very agent the release is about to dispose.\n   */\n  private readonly generations = new Map<string, number>()\n  /**\n   * Teardown still running, per key. The epoch above protects a walk that\n   * STARTED before the release; this protects the one that starts during it.\n   *\n   * A release detaches its maps and then awaits `dispose()`, and for that\n   * moment the host registry can still answer with the agent being torn down.\n   * A fresh walk arriving there finds it through `lookup`, adopts it as\n   * someone ELSE's live agent — so it will never dispose it — publishes it as\n   * the conversation's binding, and the release then destroys the object the\n   * new binding points at. Nothing about that is visible until the next\n   * message drives a disposed agent.\n   */\n  private readonly retiring = new Map<string, Promise<void>>()\n  private closed = false\n\n  /**\n   * @param scope - the conversation facet every session is keyed by.\n   * @param ladder - the host operations to walk.\n   * @param idFor - session id per conversation key; the default is the plain\n   * branding, and a workspace-aware channel injects a deriver that\n   * discriminates by directory too.\n   */\n  constructor(\n    private readonly scope: SessionScope,\n    private readonly ladder: SessionLadder,\n    private readonly idFor: (key: string) => string = sessionIdFor,\n  ) {}\n\n  /** Session ids currently bound, in insertion order. */\n  get sessionIds(): string[] {\n    return [...this.keys.keys()]\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * The live agent this store opened for one session id.\n   *\n   * The store's own record rather than the registry's: this channel created\n   * or resumed the agent, so the authoritative answer to \"is there something\n   * to drive for this conversation\" is here, not in a lookup whose publication\n   * rules belong to the host.\n   * @param sessionId - the session id to look up.\n   * @returns the agent, or undefined when this store drives no such session.\n   */\n  agentFor(sessionId: string): HostAgentHandle['agent'] | undefined {\n    const key = this.keys.get(sessionId)\n    return key === undefined ? undefined : this.opened.get(key)?.handle.agent\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * The conversation key a live session id serves.\n   * @param sessionId - a session id, as carried by a host session event.\n   * @returns the key, or undefined when this store does not drive the session.\n   */\n  keyOf(sessionId: string): string | undefined {\n    return this.keys.get(sessionId)\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Resolve the agent for one inbound message.\n   * @param msg - normalized inbound chat message.\n   * @returns the bound session, the same object for every later message of its key.\n   * @throws {Error} when this store is closed, or when no ladder rung yielded an agent.\n   */\n  async acquire(msg: NormalizedMessage): Promise<OpenedSession> {\n    return this.acquireKey(conversationKey(this.scope, msg))\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Resolve the agent for one conversation key. A loop rather than a single\n   * walk: every await is a window for a release or a switch to move the\n   * conversation on, and a result that no longer matches the key's current\n   * state is retried under the new state instead of being handed out stale.\n   * @param key - the conversation key.\n   * @returns the bound session, the same object for every later call of its key.\n   * @throws {Error} when this store is closed, or when creation genuinely fails.\n   */\n  async acquireKey(key: string): Promise<OpenedSession> {\n    for (;;) {\n      if (this.closed) throw new Error('lark-channel: sessions are closed')\n      // Before the registry is consulted, not after: a teardown in flight is\n      // exactly when `lookup` still answers with the agent being disposed.\n      const retiring = this.retiring.get(key)\n      if (retiring !== undefined) {\n        await retiring\n        continue\n      }\n      const generation = this.generation(key)\n      const bound = this.opened.get(key)\n      if (bound !== undefined) {\n        // Reusable only while it still IS this key's session: a workspace\n        // switch re-derives the id, and a stale binding is released — a second\n        // release is a no-op — before walking under the new state.\n        if (bound.handle.agent.session.id === this.idFor(key)) return bound\n        await this.release(key)\n        continue\n      }\n      let opening = this.opening.get(key)\n      if (opening === undefined) {\n        opening = this.bind(key, generation)\n        this.opening.set(key, opening)\n        // Failure clears the slot so the next message retries — but only the\n        // failure that still owns the slot, never a successor's promise.\n        opening.catch(() => {\n          if (this.opening.get(key) === opening) this.opening.delete(key)\n        })\n      }\n      let result: OpenedSession\n      try {\n        result = await opening\n      } catch (error) {\n        if (error instanceof SupersededError) continue\n        throw error\n      }\n      // Joined waiters validate what they were handed: the generation still\n      // current, the binding still published, the id still this key's.\n      if (\n        this.generation(key) === generation\n        && this.opened.get(key) === result\n        && result.handle.agent.session.id === this.idFor(key)\n      ) return result\n    }\n  }\n\n  /** The release epoch one key is currently in. */\n  private generation(key: string): number {\n    return this.generations.get(key) ?? 0\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Unbind one conversation and dispose the agent it held, so the next message\n   * walks the ladder afresh — which is what makes a workspace switch take\n   * effect. An adopted agent (another owner's) is unbound but left running:\n   * whoever created it still owns taking it down.\n   * @param key - the conversation key to release.\n   * @returns whether a binding existed.\n   */\n  async release(key: string): Promise<boolean> {\n    // A teardown already in flight IS this key's release: joining it keeps\n    // \"released\" meaning \"quiescent\" for the second caller too, instead of\n    // reporting nothing to do while an agent is still being destroyed.\n    const inFlight = this.retiring.get(key)\n    if (inFlight !== undefined) await inFlight\n    const bound = this.opened.get(key)\n    const opening = this.opening.get(key)\n    if (bound === undefined && opening === undefined) return false\n    // The epoch advances SYNCHRONOUSLY, before any await: from this statement\n    // on, every earlier walk is stale and will retry rather than hand out what\n    // is being torn down here. Detaching the maps in the same breath means a\n    // fresh acquire starts cleanly instead of joining a doomed walk.\n    this.generations.set(key, this.generation(key) + 1)\n    this.opened.delete(key)\n    if (this.opening.get(key) === opening) this.opening.delete(key)\n    if (bound !== undefined) this.keys.delete(bound.handle.agent.session.id)\n    // ONE teardown covering everything this release still has in flight, and\n    // published while it runs — an acquire arriving mid-release waits for all\n    // of it rather than racing part of it.\n    //\n    // Both halves can still be producing an agent. The\n    // detached walk is still inside `resume`/`create`, which PUBLISH to the\n    // registry before this store ever sees the handle: a fresh walk that\n    // looked there would adopt that agent as someone else's, and the stale\n    // walk — seeing the moved epoch — would then dispose the very object the\n    // new binding just took.\n    // Deferred by one microtask so the barrier is in the map BEFORE any of\n    // this runs: `dispose()` is another package's code, and one that emits\n    // synchronously could re-enter `acquireKey` while the map still said\n    // nothing was retiring.\n    const teardown = Promise.resolve().then(async () => {\n      if (bound?.owned === true) {\n        await bound.handle.dispose().catch((error: unknown) => {\n          this.ladder.report(`lark-channel: disposing the released session for ${key} failed: ${failureDetail(error)}`)\n        })\n      }\n      // A detached walk cleans up its own product: bind() sees the moved\n      // epoch, disposes what it made, and rejects as superseded.\n      if (opening !== undefined) await opening.then(() => undefined, () => undefined)\n    })\n    this.retiring.set(key, teardown)\n    try {\n      await teardown\n    } finally {\n      if (this.retiring.get(key) === teardown) this.retiring.delete(key)\n    }\n    return true\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Stop accepting new work and dispose every owned agent. [result.reason as unknown] : [])\n    if (failures.length > 0) throw new AggregateError(failures, 'lark-channel: session disposal failed')\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Walk the ladder for one key and publish the result under it.\n   * @param key - the conversation key being bound.\n   * @returns the bound session.\n   * @throws {Error} when the ladder yielded nothing, or when the store closed\n   * mid-walk — the disposal sweep has already run, so the agent it produced is\n   * taken down here instead of outliving its owner.\n   */\n  /**\n   * Walk the ladder for one key and publish the result — unless the world\n   * moved while walking. Reporting it keeps a corrupt session log\n      // from passing silently as first contact.\n      this.ladder.report(\n        `lark-channel: resuming session for ${key} failed, starting a new one: ${failureDetail(error)}`,\n      )\n    }\n    return { handle: await this.ladder.create(sessionId), owned: true }\n  }\n}\n"

      "content": "/**\n * Per-conversation workspaces. `/cd` points one conversation at a directory,\n * and the conversation's session id is derived from BOTH facts, so every\n * (conversation × directory) pair owns a durable session of its own. That turns\n * a host constraint into the feature: a session's cwd is fixed at creation, so\n * \"switching\" is really reaching a different session — and coming back to a\n * directory resumes the context that was built there instead of erasing it.\n *\n * The mapping persists through the host settings service, in the same section\n * that already holds onboarded credentials, so a restarted process routes every\n * conversation to the session it served before. Entries never need deletion —\n * the persistence layer deep-merges patches — so \"back to the default\" is an\n * explicit marker value rather than an absent key.\n * @module dsh-lark-channel/workspace\n */\n\nimport { createHash } from 'node:crypto'\nimport { realpathSync, statSync } from 'node:fs'\nimport { homedir } from 'node:os'\nimport { basename, dirname, isAbsolute, resolve, sep } from 'node:path'\nimport { epochSessionId } from './epoch.ts'\nimport { sessionIdFor } from './session.ts'\n\n/** Switch or show this conversation's workspace. Channel-owned: it needs no agent. */\nexport const CD_COMMAND = 'cd'\n\n/** List the workspaces this channel knows. Channel-owned: it needs no agent. */\nexport const WS_COMMAND = 'ws'\n\n/** Entry value marking \"explicitly the default\": a deep-merged patch cannot delete a key. */\nconst DEFAULT_MARKER = ''\n\n/**\n * Verdict on one directory: its canonical path, or why it cannot be a workspace.\n * Injectable so command tests need no real filesystem.\n */\nexport type WorkspaceProbe = (path: string) => { readonly canonical: string } | { readonly error: string }\n\n/** The real-filesystem probe: the directory must exist, and spellings collapse to one. */\nexport const probeDirectory: WorkspaceProbe = (path) => {\n  try {\n    if (!statSync(path).isDirectory()) return { error: '不是目录' }\n    return { canonical: realpathSync(path) }\n  } catch {\n    return { error: '目录不存在' }\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Expand a leading `~` against the operating-system home, the one path shorthand\n * a phone keyboard makes worth supporting.\n * @param input - the operator's path input.\n * @param home - substitutable home directory.\n * @returns the expanded path, or the input untouched.\n */\nexport function expandHome(input: string, home = homedir()): string {\n  if (input === '~') return home\n  if (input.startsWith('~/')) return resolve(home, input.slice(2))\n  return input\n}\n\n/**\n * Why a directory can never be a workspace, however permissive the roots are.\n * These are the directories a `/cd` typo or a lazy shortcut lands on — and an\n * agent whose sandbox writes \"the workspace\" must not have that be the\n * filesystem root or someone's entire home.\n * @param canonical - the canonicalized candidate.\n * @param home - the home directory, canonicalized by the caller's probe.\n * @returns the refusal, or undefined when the directory is specific enough.\n */\nexport function forbiddenReason(canonical: string, home = homedir()): string | undefined {\n  if (dirname(canonical) === canonical) return '不能把文件系统根目录设为工作区'\n  if (canonical === home) return '不能把 Home 根目录设为工作区，请选更具体的子目录'\n  if (canonical === dirname(home)) return '不能把用户目录的父级设为工作区'\n  return undefined\n}\n\n/**\n * Whether a path falls under one of the configured roots. An empty list allows\n * anywhere: the platform already decides who can reach the bot, and this knob\n * only narrows what those people may point it at.\n * @param path - canonical candidate directory.\n * @param roots - allowed directory prefixes.\n * @returns true when allowed.\n */\nexport function withinRoots(path: string, roots: readonly string[]): boolean {\n  if (roots.length === 0) return true\n  return roots.some((root) => {\n    const resolved = resolve(root)\n    return path === resolved || path.startsWith(resolved.endsWith(sep) ? resolved : `${resolved}${sep}`)\n  })\n}\n\n/**\n * The session id one conversation-and-workspace pair owns. The default\n * workspace keeps the historical plain id, so existing conversations keep their\n * sessions across this feature's arrival; an override appends a digest of the\n * canonical directory, so two spellings of one directory reach one session and\n * two directories never share.\n * @param key - conversation key.\n * @param overridePath - canonical override directory, absent for the default.\n * @returns the branded session id.\n */\nexport function workspaceSessionId(key: string, overridePath?: string, prefix?: string): string {\n  const base = sessionIdFor(key, prefix)\n  if (overridePath === undefined) return base\n  return `${base}--${createHash('sha256').update(overridePath).digest('hex').slice(0, 10)}`\n}\n\n/** What one `/cd` attempt concluded. */\nexport type SwitchResult =\n  | {\n      readonly ok: true\n      /** The conversation's workspace after the switch. */\n      readonly path: string\n      /** False when the conversation was already there. */\n      readonly changed: boolean\n      /** Whether the target is the deployment default. */\n      readonly toDefault: boolean\n      /** Whether the mapping survives a restart. */\n      readonly durable: boolean\n    }\n  | { readonly ok: false; readonly reason: string }\n\n/** Construction options for {@link ChatWorkspaces}. */\nexport interface ChatWorkspacesOptions {\n  /** The deployment default directory (resolved, not necessarily canonical). */\n  readonly defaultPath: string\n  /** Persisted conversation-key → directory entries; {@link DEFAULT_MARKER} means default. */\n  readonly entries?: Record<string, string> | undefined\n  /** Directory prefixes `/cd` may enter; empty allows anywhere. */\n  readonly roots?: readonly string[] | undefined\n  /** Deep-merge one patch into the plugin's settings section; false = not composed. */\n  readonly persist?: ((patch: { chatWorkspaces: Record<string, string> }) => Promise<boolean>) | undefined\n  /** Operator console line. */\n  readonly report?: ((line: string) => void) | undefined\n  /** Directory verdicts; tests substitute one. */\n  readonly probe?: WorkspaceProbe | undefined\n  /** Home for `~` expansion and the forbidden-directory rules; tests substitute one. */\n  readonly home?: string | undefined\n  /** Prefix this row's session ids carry; absent keeps the original one. */\n  readonly sessionPrefix?: string | undefined\n  /**\n   * How many times a conversation has started over, by the id it derives at\n   * epoch zero. Absent keeps every conversation on its first.\n   */\n  readonly epochOf?: ((baseId: string) => number) | undefined\n  /**\n   * Directories known outside this channel — the host workspace registry's\n   * listing, when the deployment composes one. What `/ws` shows and what a\n   * bare-name `/cd` can reach, so a chat can discover every project its human\n   * already uses with the host instead of memorizing paths.\n   */\n  readonly known?: (() => readonly string[]) | undefined\n}\n\n/**\n * The per-conversation workspace state: which directory each conversation is\n * pointed at, the session id that pair owns, and the `/cd` transition between\n * them. Pure state plus injected effects, so tests drive it without a\n * filesystem or a settings service.\n */\nexport class ChatWorkspaces {\n  private readonly entries: Map<string, string>\n  private readonly defaultPath: string\n  /** The default's canonical form, for deciding that a `/cd` target IS the default. */\n  private readonly defaultCanonical: string\n  private readonly roots: readonly string[]\n  private readonly persist: (patch: { chatWorkspaces: Record<string, string> }) => Promise<boolean>\n  private readonly report: (line: string) => void\n  private readonly probe: WorkspaceProbe\n  private readonly home: string | undefined\n  private readonly known: () => readonly string[]\n  private readonly sessionPrefix: string | undefined\n  private readonly epochOf: (baseId: string) => number\n  /** The non-durable warning is orientation; once is enough. */\n  private warnedNotDurable = false\n\n  constructor(options: ChatWorkspacesOptions) {\n    this.defaultPath = options.defaultPath\n    this.roots = options.roots ?? []\n    this.persist = options.persist ?? (async () => false)\n    this.report = options.report ?? (() => {})\n    this.probe = options.probe ?? probeDirectory\n    this.home = options.home\n    this.known = options.known ??
